findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning data at rest in the RDS instance is not encrypted, violating encryption-at-rest requirements for sensitive data.
publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the MySQL database instance directly to the internet and significantly increasing attack surface.

The master username is hard-coded to 'admin' and the password is sourced from var.password with no secrets manager integration, and this same secret is embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, risking credential leakage via instance metadata, console output, or state files.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database username and password in plaintext within a PHP file on disk, which is retrievable via the EC2 instance metadata service (IMDS) and readable by anyone with instance, console, or Terraform state access.

The IAM policy grants full wildcard actions (s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*) on all resources (Resource: "*") to the EC2 instance role, violating least privilege. This is especially severe because the role is attached to an EC2 instance that is likely internet-facing, so compromise of the instance yields near-account-wide access.

findings.issue_category: undefined/unreviewable security group referenced by internet-facing instance
findings.description: aws_instance.db_app attaches vpc_security_group_ids referencing aws_security_group.web-node, which is not defined in this file; combined with the instance's user_data serving a public web app, its ingress rules could not be verified and warrant review, but cannot be confirmed as a vulnerability from this file alone.
